newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour sends voters no tax rise pledge.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour sends voters no tax rise pledge.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour party on Friday mailed a million voters a pledge not to raise the basic or top rates of tax if it wins the election due in the next three months.

In another bid to drive home the message that Labour is no longer a "tax-and-spend" party and to counter Conservative party attacks, economics spokesman Gordon Brown sent a personalised letter to a million voters in key marginal seats.
In the letter, Brown repeated five pledges he has made in a series of key speeches and news conferences.

Labour would set tough rules for public spending, hold basic and top rates of income tax unchanged, introduce a new lower starting tax rate of ten percent, cut value added tax on heating to five percent and only make affordable commitments.
"My first principle of taxation is that hard work ought to be rewarded rather than penalised...," Brown said. "My second principle is that tax should be fair to hard-working families.
With the election due by May, Labour is around 20 points up in opinion polls. But it is still sensitive to charges that it is untested in government after 18 years of Conservative rule.

As well as the letter, Labour officials said they were also sending a four-page tabloid "newspaper" to another two million voters setting out the party's promises on tax, health, education and other key areas.
